description:
SECTION: Documentation as contract

CONTRACT RISK
Three fields on Message all encode some aspect of "did this message
get delivered?":

  src/message.rs  Message.delivery_state: DeliveryState
                  required, enum: Pending / Delivered / Failed /
                  Received / Other(String)

  src/message.rs  Message.delivered_at: Option<UTCDate>
                  optional timestamp

  src/message.rs  Message.delivery_receipts: Option<HashMap<String, DeliveryReceipt>>
                  optional per-recipient receipts, each carrying its
                  own delivered_at / device_delivered_at / read_at /
                  read_disposition

Each field's doc says only "The `<name>` property
(draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11)." There is no statement of which
field is authoritative when they disagree, or what the relationship
between them is supposed to be:

- If delivery_state == DeliveryState::Pending, can delivered_at still
  be Some(...)? Should it be?
- If delivery_receipts is Some(_) and one or more receipts have a
  delivered_at, must delivered_at on the parent Message also be
  Some(_)?
- If delivery_state == Delivered but delivery_receipts is None, what
  does the caller infer? "We don't track per-recipient" vs "All
  receipts are pending"?
- Same question stack for read_at vs delivery_receipts.read_at.

WHAT BREAKS FOR CALLERS
A caller writing a delivery-status UI must either:
  (a) consult all three fields and decide its own primacy rules
      (likely diverging from other implementations), or
  (b) consult one field and ignore the others (silently mis-reporting
      when they conflict).

This is doubly important because DeliveryState carries an
Other(String) catch-all (JMAP-ly0n already covers forward-compat for
result enums) — a state the caller doesn't know how to interpret
combined with timestamps it doesn't know how to weight is a
defensive-code minefield.

The mode-prompt review did not flag this. None of JMAP-ly0n.1
through JMAP-ly0n.13 addresses the multi-source-of-truth question
for Message delivery fields.

RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION
Add a #[doc] block at the top of struct Message (or on
DeliveryState) that establishes the contract:

  /// # Delivery status fields
  ///
  /// Three fields encode delivery status; their relationship is:
  ///
  /// - `delivery_state` is the *summary* the server has computed
  ///   (server-side aggregate). Consult this first.
  /// - `delivered_at` is *the* time the server considers the message
  ///   delivered to the recipient endpoint; absent until
  ///   delivery_state >= Delivered.
  /// - `delivery_receipts` is the per-recipient breakdown. When
  ///   present, it is authoritative for per-recipient state and
  ///   `delivered_at` is derived from it (e.g. earliest, latest, or
  ///   majority — spec must say which).
  ///
  /// (Adjust to whatever the draft actually mandates.)

This belongs in the spec first; the API doc should track the spec
once the spec settles it. Until then, surface the question as a
draft-level open issue and document it on the type so callers know
the field semantics are not yet pinned down.

ORACLE
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §4.11 (Message); JMAP-ly0n.1 (SenderId
sentinel) is the closest precedent for "wire-shape ambiguity needs
explicit documentation".
title: Message delivery state has three sources of truth without doc-stated primacy (delivery_state, delivered_at, delivery_receipts)
